assessment.nobel_worthiness: Alternating-offers bargaining supplied a parsimonious and enduring foundation for the analysis of strategic negotiation and market bargaining.
assessment.attribution: Rubinstein is central to the alternating-offers framework; Wolinsky is an appropriate principal credit for bargaining in market settings.
assessment.maturity: The theoretical contribution is long established and has generated extensive subsequent work across economics.
uncertainties: The proposed discovery combines a canonical bargaining model with a broader market-bargaining literature, making the precise prize citation consequential.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ambiguity-sensitive decision theory transformed the treatment of choice under incomplete probabilistic knowledge and remains foundational.
assessment.attribution: Gilboa is a core architect of maxmin expected utility, while Epstein is a principal contributor to axiomatic approaches to ambiguity.
assessment.maturity: The concepts have had decades of theoretical development and broad application in finance, macroeconomics and decision theory.
uncertainties: A single citation spanning Choquet and maxmin traditions may leave difficult choices about the complete set of essential contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Experimental markets and behavioural game experiments made controlled evidence central to the study of institutions and strategic behaviour.
assessment.attribution: Plott and Holt were formative in experimental market design and analysis; Camerer is a leading contributor to behavioural game theory and strategic reasoning.
assessment.maturity: This is a mature research programme with durable methods, replications and influence well beyond experimental economics.
uncertainties: The candidate description encompasses several experimental traditions and more eligible contributors than the prize limit permits.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Network analysis has supplied powerful tools for understanding social learning, link formation and strategic interaction among connected agents.
assessment.attribution: Jackson, Kranton and Goyal each made central, complementary contributions to economic network theory.
assessment.maturity: The field is well developed and influential, with methods and insights adopted across microeconomics and related disciplines.
uncertainties: The breadth of network economics complicates a sharply delimited attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Bayesian persuasion and information design recast information provision as an explicit design problem with wide applications.
assessment.attribution: Bergemann and Kamenica are the clearest central contributors to the modern persuasion framework.
assessment.maturity: The programme has rapidly become a major component of information economics and mechanism design.
uncertainties: Its comparatively recent expansion leaves less time to assess its ultimate durability than older theoretical candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Work on reciprocity, fairness and inequity aversion changed economic accounts of cooperation, contracts and incentives.
assessment.attribution: Fehr and Falk provided influential experimental evidence, while Fehr and Schmidt supplied a seminal formal account of inequity aversion.
assessment.maturity: The contribution has had sustained theoretical and empirical influence across labour, organisational and behavioural economics.
uncertainties: The empirical and theoretical strands have overlapping but not identical principal authorship.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification made credible inference possible when data and assumptions cannot justify point identification.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the pivotal intellectual source; Tamer is a principal contributor to moment-inequality methods.
assessment.maturity: The approach is mature and has become an important standard for transparent empirical work under weak assumptions.
uncertainties: The proposed cluster includes several methodological branches whose relative centrality may warrant further assessment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm-heterogeneity models reshaped the analysis of trade, selection, productivity and the distribution of gains from globalization.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is central to the canonical firm-selection model; Helpman and Redding made major complementary contributions to its theoretical development and applications.
assessment.maturity: The framework is deeply embedded in international-trade research and has generated a substantial empirical literature.
uncertainties: The connection between the broad literature and a limited set of laureates requires careful delimitation.
